name: MT3608
description: High-frequency (1.2MHz) step-up (boost) converter in SOT-23-6, the chip on the common small blue boost modules. Input 2-24V, output up to 28V, internal 4A-limit switch (~2A typical usable output). Sets output with an external feedback divider against a 0.6V reference.

pins.name: SW
pins.description: switch node; connects to the inductor

pins.name: FB
pins.description: feedback; regulates to 0.6V via the external divider

pins.name: EN
pins.description: enable; high to turn on, low to shut down

extra.Iq: 100uA typ (200uA max) PFM mode; 1.6mA typ (2.2mA max) PWM mode
extra.SW Ron: 80 mOhm typ (150 max) -- internal switch on-resistance, the switcher analog of linear dropout

typical_application: Boost a single Li-ion or USB 5V up to 9/12V. Vout = 0.6 * (1 + R1/R2) with R1 from OUT to FB. Inductor on SW, Schottky to the output.
gotchas: boost converters cannot output below their input; with EN high there is always a DC path (through the inductor and diode) from IN to OUT
the 4A figure is the internal switch current LIMIT, not output current; usable output is closer to ~2A and falls as the step-up ratio rises
pin 6 is NC; do not rely on it for anything
needs a suitable inductor and a fast Schottky catch diode; cheap modules vary in quality
